headline: Five-Day Mission Restores Sight for 345 in Jamaica
meta_description: Duke University ophthalmologists partnered with local doctors at Kingston Public Hospital to perform free cataract surgeries for 345 patients.
summary_short: A surgical team from Duke University and local doctors restored vision for 345 people during a five-day cataract surgery mission at Kingston Public Hospital in Jamaica.
body:
A five-day cataract surgery mission at Kingston Public Hospital in Jamaica restored sight for 345 people who otherwise lacked access to care. Ophthalmologists from Duke University partnered with local doctors to deliver the free procedures, addressing a critical gap in eye care for the community.

The collaboration between American specialists and Jamaica's medical staff demonstrates how targeted international partnerships can expand surgical capacity in underserved regions. Many of the patients who received treatment had been living with vision loss that surgery could correct—a reality that often goes unaddressed in areas with limited resources.

By bringing together expertise from both sides, the mission provided not only immediate relief to hundreds of individuals but also strengthened local surgical capabilities, leaving a lasting impact on the hospital's ability to serve its patients.
quick_facts: 345 people regained sight during the mission
Duke University ophthalmologists led the effort
Surgery took place at Kingston Public Hospital, Jamaica
All procedures were provided free of charge
